title: Nested cellular automaton patterns can be computed in logarithmic time

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Nested cellular automaton patterns can be computed in logarithmic time

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: For cellular automata with nested behavior such as elementary rules 60 and 188, the color of a cell after t steps can be found in about log2(t) steps from the base-2 digits of its position, rather than by tracing all t steps.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In general, to find the color of a cell after t steps of rule 188 or rule 60 evolution takes about Log[2, t] steps.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Computational Irreducibility” (from p. 737), p. 744. Scope: elementary cellular automata rules 60 and 188, and nested patterns generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-17: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.98

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The named-rule statement is precise, reproducible, and amenable to a short algebraic proof plus exhaustive finite checks. Public rule definitions contain all necessary inputs, and the result cleanly distinguishes logarithmic prediction from stepwise evolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Implement rules 60 and 188 and the digit-based cell algorithm, verify equality over extensive positions and times, and prove the recurrence computes the same cell in O(log t) arithmetic steps. A mismatching cell or superlogarithmic required recurrence would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The extension from the named rules to nested patterns generally is broader than the exact result.

The cost model for arithmetic on t-bit integers must be stated.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Rule 60 is binomial coefficients modulo 2, readable from base-2 digits, and rule 188 has an explicit digit-automaton of the same logarithmic length. Both are short programs a public simulator can compare with direct evolution. The stated scope is these two rules and nested patterns of the same kind, which the same style of check covers.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For rules 60 and 188, compute the color at a cell after t steps both by direct evolution and by the base-2 digit procedure that runs for about log2(t) steps. Agreement, backed by a correctness argument for the digit rule, confirms the claim; a mismatch refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Direct checks reach large finite t; the claim for every t is closed by a correctness argument for the digit procedure.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.9

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: For elementary rules 60 and 188 started from a single black cell, the colour of the cell at position x after t steps is a 2-automatic function of (t, x): a fixed finite automaton reading the base-2 digits of t and x in parallel (one digit pair per step, hence about log2(t) steps) outputs the colour, and this automaton can be constructed from the pattern and reproduces it exactly, including at times not used in its construction.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py evolves each rule from a single black cell to a 4096 x 4096 array A(t, x). (i) For levels k = 0..7 it extracts every 2-kernel element A(2^k t + r, 2^k x + s) on a 32 x 32 window and counts cumulative distinct elements. (ii) From the 2048 x 2048 sub-pattern it builds the automaton whose states are the distinct 64 x 64 kernel windows (levels k <= 5), with transition (k, r, s) -> (k+1, r + 2^k dt, s + 2^k dx) on digit pair (dt, dx), checks that no state has conflicting or undefined transitions, then runs the automaton on the least-significant-first binary digits of (t, x) for all 16,777,216 cells of the 4096 x 4096 array (12 digit pairs) and compares with A; it also stops the automaton after bitlen(t) digit pairs and compares on the 8,390,656 cells with x <= t. Controls 30, 110 (mirrored), 90 and 150 (right halves) are treated identically. Run time about 30 s.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered, for each of rules 60 and 188: (i) the number of distinct 2-kernel elements A(2^k t + r, 2^k x + s), compared on a 64 x 64 window, saturates: the cumulative count over levels k <= 5 equals the cumulative count over all levels k <= K - 6 of a 2^K x 2^K pattern with K = 11 (i.e. no new element appears beyond level 5), and that count is at most 64; (ii) the finite automaton whose states are those kernel elements and whose transitions on a digit pair (dt, dx) go from element (k, r, s) to (k+1, r + 2^k dt, s + 2^k dx) is consistent (every representative of a state yields the same target state for each digit pair) and, run on the least-significant-first binary digits of (t, x), reproduces 100% of the cells of an independently evolved 2^12 x 2^12 pattern (t < 4096), three quarters of which lie outside the K = 11 construction range; (iii) the number of automaton steps for a cell at time t equals the number of binary digits of t, i.e. floor(log2 t) + 1.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: for rule 60 or rule 188 the kernel count keeps growing beyond level 5 (no saturation) or exceeds 64, or the automaton is inconsistent, or any cell of the 2^12 x 2^12 pattern disagrees with the automaton's output. Control rules 30 and 110 (not nested) are expected to fail (i) and (ii); if they passed, the test would be too weak and the verdict would be 'inconclusive' with reason 'not-operationalizable'.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: cells (of 2 x 16,777,216) where the digit automaton disagrees with direct evolution, rules 60 and 188

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Wolfram's statement (p. 744) is that the colour of a cell of rule 60 or rule 188 after t steps can be found by a cellular automaton acting on the base-2 digit sequences of the cell's coordinates (6 colours for rule 60, 12 for rule 188) in about log2(t) steps instead of t steps. The finite-automaton formulation used here is equivalent: a two-dimensional pattern computable from the binary digits of (t, x) by a finite-state device is a 2-automatic double sequence, whose characterization (Cobham, Salon) is finiteness of its 2-kernel; the automaton's step count is the number of digit pairs, floor(log2 t) + 1. The exact state counts Wolfram quotes (6 and 12) refer to his particular digit-CA encoding and are not tested; only the existence of a finite digit automaton and its logarithmic step count are. Rules 60 and 188 both grow only to the right from a single black cell at x = 0, so A(t, x) is defined for 0 <= x <= t and taken as 0 for x > t. For the controls, the right half (x >= 0) of rule 30, 90 and 150 and the mirror image of rule 110 are used. The clause 'nested patterns generally' is addressed only through rules 90 and 150 as further nested examples.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
Elementary rules 60 and 188 from a single black cell, 4096 steps, 4096 columns (generated by analysis.py)

Elementary rules 30, 110 (mirrored), 90 and 150 from a single black cell, 4096 steps, right half x >= 0 (generated by analysis.py)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The pre-registered saturation criterion (i) as written ('cumulative count over k <= 5 equals the count over k <= K - 6 with K = 11') is vacuous because K - 6 = 5; it was applied in the intended stronger form on the 4096 x 4096 pattern with a 32 x 32 window (levels up to 7): for rules 60 and 188 no new kernel element appears after level 1 and 2 respectively (2 and 7 distinct elements), while the controls 30 and 110 gain 4^k new elements at every level.

The automaton was built from the 2048 x 2048 pattern and reproduces all 16,777,216 cells of the 4096 x 4096 pattern, 12,582,912 of which were not used in its construction; agreement for all t is implied by 2-automaticity but was verified only up to t = 4095.

Wolfram's exact state counts (6 colours for rule 60, 12 for rule 188) belong to his particular digit cellular automaton and were not reproduced; the kernel automata found here have 2 and 7 states. The claim's extension to 'nested patterns generally' was checked only on rules 90 and 150 (4 states each).
